title: Stage 5: The performance pass
summary: Remove the N+1 from a member's loans, page overdue loans with a keyset cursor, and index for it.

steps.title: Count the commands
body: Your API works. Now make it **fast**, measurably. From this stage on the tests count every SQL command your server runs during a request (they listen to EF Core's diagnostic events, so you do not need to change anything for that).

The quick `GET /members/{id}/loans` from stage 4 probably runs one query for the loans, then more for each loan's book and author: 1 + 2N commands. A member with 30 loans costs 61 round trips. Rewrite it as **one projection** (plus, if you like, one cheap existence check for the 404).
And the front desk needs a list of **overdue loans**: there can be thousands, so page it with a **keyset cursor** on `(Due, Id)`, and add an index that matches the query.

steps.prompt: The overdue query is `WHERE NOT Returned AND Due < @today ORDER BY Due, Id` plus the cursor condition on `(Due, Id)`. Which index serves it best?
steps.explain: Equality column first (`Returned`), then the range and sort columns in sort order (`Due`, `Id`). The database seeks to `Returned = 0`, walks the `Due` range already sorted, and can resume exactly at the cursor.

steps.prompt: How many commands for a member with N loans?
items: `db.Loans.Where(l => l.MemberId == id).Select(l => new { l.Book.Title, Author = l.Book.Author.Name }).ToList()`
`foreach (var l in loans) await db.Entry(l).Reference(x => x.Book).LoadAsync();`
steps.explain: Projections and `Include` fetch everything in one round trip. Anything that runs a query or a load per loan is N+1.

steps.title: Make it fast
prompt: - Rewrite `GET /members/{id}/loans` (same response) to run **at most 2 SQL commands** whatever the number of loans: a projection from `db.Loans` that reaches `l.Book.Title` and `l.Book.Author.Name`.
- Add `GET /loans/overdue?today=2026-12-10&size=2&afterDue=&afterId=`: loans **not returned** with `Due` before `today`, ordered by `Due`, then id, as
`size` defaults to 10 (1..50). With `afterDue` and `afterId`, continue after that loan. **One** SQL command per page, no `Skip`: fetch `size + 1` rows to know whether there is a next page.

await Post(http, "/loans", new { bookId = 2, memberId = 1, due = "2026-12-05" });

Dojo.Check("...in at most 2 SQL commands, whatever the number of loans", dojoCount <= 2, $"it ran {dojoCount} commands");
Dojo.Eq("overdue page 1: oldest due first", "Dune|Earthsea", Each(Field(dojoP1, "items"), "title"));

Dojo.Check("...in one SQL command", dojoOverdueCount == 1, $"it ran {dojoOverdueCount} commands");

Dojo.Eq("returned and future loans are not overdue", 0, Field(dojoEarly, "items").ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array ? Field(dojoEarly, "items").GetArrayLength() : -1);
Dojo.Check("GET /books stays at 2 commands (count + page)", DojoSql.Commands <= 2, $"it ran {DojoSql.Commands} commands");
static async Task<HttpResponseMessage> Post(HttpClient http, string url, object body) => await http.PostAsJsonAsync(url, body);
static async Task<string?> Id(HttpResponseMessage r) => DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(r), "id");
static string Each(JsonElement json, string prop) =>
json.ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Array ? string.Join("|", json.EnumerateArray().Select(x => DojoWeb.Prop(x, prop))) : "(not an array)";
static JsonElement Field(JsonElement json, string name)
foreach (var p in json.EnumerateObject()) if (string.Equals(p.Name, name, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)) return p.Value;
public void OnNext(KeyValuePair<string, object?> e) { if (e.Key == "Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Database.Command.CommandExecuted") Interlocked.Increment(ref Commands); }

forbid.message: Pages overdue loans with a cursor, not Skip

hints: `.Select(l => new { LoanId = l.Id, l.Book.Title, Author = l.Book.Author.Name, l.Due, l.Returned })`
Cursor condition: `l.Due > due || (l.Due == due && l.Id > last)`.
`DateOnly today` and `DateOnly? afterDue` bind from the query string.
